articles.headline: NFL Week 4's best arrivals, led by Cleveland Browns mascot
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: クリーブランド・ブラウンズのマスコットを筆頭とする、NFL第4週の最高の会場入りショット
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、毎週のスタジアム入りを自身のためのファッションショーへと変え続けています。
articles.body:
Week 4 of the NFL season has arrived, and the calendar has officially flipped to October. But sweater weather hasn't quite followed everywhere. 

Unseasonable heat out West could keep layers light for another week, while cooler temperatures settling in across the East are opening the door for more fall-ready fits. That means players have plenty of options as they make their Week 4 entrances. With three weeks of looks already in the books, personal styles are also starting to take shape around the league. Some players have leaned into statement pieces, while others have kept things clean and understated.

From warm-weather looks to seasonal layers, Week 4 brings another round of game-day style as the calendar officially turns to fall.

Thursday night's fashion

Players and coaches aren't the only ones showing off their style pregame. Mascots get in on the tunnel fits, too. This week, Brownie the Elf was ready to rock for Cleveland's Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Game, channeling Prince in a purple jacket with a matching guitar.

articles.headline: Brian Flores and his dominant Vikings defense take on the winless Dolphins, the team he once coached
articles.description: — Brian Flores has become one of the most impactful and prominent assistant coaches in the
articles.headlineJa: ブライアン・フローレス率いる強力なバイキングス守備陣が、古巣である未勝利のドルフィンズと対戦
articles.descriptionJa: — ブライアン・フローレスは、最も影響力があり目立った活躍を見せるアシスタントコーチのひとりとなっています。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Brian Flores has become one of the most impactful and prominent assistant coaches in the NFL over four seasons as defensive coordinator of the Minnesota Vikings, with his knack for play calling and a gift for maximizing the group's strengths.


              Flores might be doing his best work yet this year with the undefeated Vikings, who have allowed the second-fewest points in the league. He'll have the opportunity on Sunday to show off his tricks to his old team, the winless Miami Dolphins.


              Fired after a three-season run as their head coach, Flores sued the NFL a month later in allegation of racially discriminatory hiring practices in a landmark case that's still in the court system four years later and awaits a trial sometime in 2027. Even if the Dolphins roster has only two players left from his last team in 2021 and his replacement Mike McDaniel was fired after last season, owner Stephen Ross remains in control of the club.


              If Flores has any strong feelings about facing the Dolphins, though, he's keeping those to himself, other than an eagerness to catch up before the game with the dozens of support staffers he's still friendly with.


              “I'm the same every week,” Flores said. “It's never about me. It's always about our team, and so the preparation's going to be the same.”


              The Vikings defense has been especially ready this season, with league-best rates in sacks per pass attempt, touchdowns allowed inside the 20-yard line, and third down conversions. The foundation for Flores has long begun with an unwavering trust in his players.


              “I tell them all the time, when people turn on the Vikings, I hope they see a team that really is connected and is having fun playing ball," Flores said. “I think we're doing that.”


              The Dolphins, with star running back De'Vone Achane done for the season with a torn ACL and quarterback Malik Willis making just his 10th career start, will have a tough task amid the deafening roar of the crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium in trying to identify and block all those creative and unpredictable sets and rushes.


              “You just can’t get really scared of it," rookie guard Kadyn Proctor said. "Just have to be locked in to the slants and to the blitzes and really just focus on doing our one-eleventh, focus on our job.”


              Need to know
              Miami (0-3) at Minnesota (3-0).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:05 p.m. EDT, CBS.


              Latest odds: Vikings by 10½.


              Against the spread: Dolphins 0-3; Vikings 3-0.


              Last week: Dolphins lost to the Chiefs 24-10; Vikings beat the Buccaneers 23-16.


              Last meeting: Vikings beat the Dolphins 24-16 on Oct. 16, 2022, in Miami. 


              Series record: Dolphins lead 8-6.


              Matchup to watch
              Vikings OLB Dallas Turner vs. Dolphins LT Patrick Paul.

articles.headline: Burrow seeks to stay unbeaten vs Lawrence as Bengals host Jaguars in matchup of 2-1 teams
articles.description: Joe Burrow has gotten the better of Trevor Lawrence whenever their teams have met.
articles.headlineJa: 2勝1敗同士が激突、ベンガルズがジャガーズを迎え撃つ中でバロウはローレンス相手の無敗維持を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: ジョー・バロウは、チーム同士が対戦するたびにトレバー・ローレンスを上回る成績を収めています。
articles.body:
Joe Burrow has gotten the better of Trevor Lawrence whenever their teams have met. 


              Burrow is hoping that trend continues on Sunday when his Cincinnati Bengals host Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in a matchup of 2-1 teams.


              Burrow is 3-0 in starts against Lawrence. The first was in the College Football Playoff national title game in the 2019 season when he threw for 463 yards and accounted for all six touchdowns in LSU's 42-25 victory over Clemson.


              The most recent time Burrow faced the Jaguars though is one he would like to forget. The franchise quarterback suffered a turf toe injury during the second quarter of last season's Week 2 game while being sacked by Jaguars defensive tackle Arik Armstead.


              Even though the Bengals rallied for a 31-27 victory behind Jake Browning, Burrow missed the next nine games after having surgery on his left big toe. The Bengals season imploded as they lost eight of nine.


              Burrow's focus though is making sure Cincinnati gets back on track after a loss at Pittsburgh despite passing for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Cincinnati was in Steelers' territory during the fourth quarter when Burrow fumbled after being sacked by Derrick Harmon.


              Burrow will face a Jaguars defense that is second in pressure rate this season.


              “They’re deep. Their two edge rushers — Armstead and DaVon (Hamilton) are really good. All those guys can play really good football, get pressure on the quarterback, stop the run,” Burrow said. “Then the rest of their defense plays with their roles really well, understands what they’re trying to do with their coverages.”


              The Jaguars' defense has picked off a pass in eight straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL, and has allowed a league-low 36 points this season.


              Cincinnati's defense also has plenty of questions going into the game. After strong games against Tampa Bay and Houston, the Bengals reverted back to the level of the past couple of seasons against the Steelers with missed tackles and lapses on long pass plays.


              Lawrence has 65 completions of at least 20 yards since the start of last season, third most in the AFC. The Bengals allowed five last week.


              “Things have changed and I think they’ve figured out kind of what they’re good at. And in some ways I think it’s kind of simplified," Lawrence said of the Bengals, the only AFC team he hasn't defeated.


              "I think sometimes that’s the hardest thing to go against is a really well-coached defense that might not bring a ton of pressures and all those things and have guys running free, but they’re just always in the right spot at the right time and you got to really earn every run, every completion, all those things. I think they’re doing a good job of that right now.”

articles.headline: Henry is on Baltimore's side now as the Ravens host the Titans in a series where road teams flourish
articles.description: — The last two times the Tennessee Titans played at Baltimore were in 2020. Derrick Henry was on their side then, and boy was he decisive.
articles.headlineJa: アウェイチームが得意とするカードでレイブンズがタイタンズを迎え撃つ中、ヘンリーは今やボルティモアの味方に
articles.descriptionJa: — テネシー・タイタンズが最後にボルティモアで試合を行った過去2回は2020年でした。当時、デリック・ヘンリーは彼らの味方であり、実に決定的な働きを見せました。
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — The last two times the Tennessee Titans played at Baltimore were in 2020. Derrick Henry was on their side then, and boy was he decisive.


              He rushed for 195 yards as the Titans beat the Ravens in a playoff game that January. Then Tennessee returned in November and topped Baltimore in overtime on a 29-yard touchdown run by Henry.


              So much has changed since.


              When the Ravens host Tennessee on Sunday, Henry will be on the opposite sideline, having left the Titans via free agency in 2024. Tennessee is 6-31 since his departure. Henry's tenure with the Titans almost feels like a different football lifetime. Tennessee even unveiled new logos earlier this year.


              “They got a whole different thing going now,” Henry said. “Going to be a crazy moment to be playing against the team that I came in the league playing for. But I’m not trying to make too much of it.”


              The Ravens (2-1) are back from Brazil after a pulsating win over Dallas in Rio de Janeiro. The Titans (0-3) have shown few signs of progress this season, aside from a competitive loss to Philadelphia. Baltimore has lost four straight home games dating to last season. If the Ravens can't snap that skid now, then when?


              On the other hand, this has been an unusual series. The last time the teams met was in London in 2023, and Baltimore won. In the 26 other games between the Titans and Ravens, the road team has won 15 times. That includes all five playoff meetings.


              “We can’t dwell on the past too much. Like I said, it is a week-to-week league, and screw whatever happened in the past,” Baltimore safety Kyle Hamilton said. “We are trying to win football games here and now, and I think we want to have the stadium rocking. We want to have fans that support us, have confidence in us, believe in us, give them a reason to come out, be loud, have something to cheer for at the game and leave that stadium happy. A lot of the past few games, nobody has left that stadium happy unless you were from the other team. So, it is up to us to fix that and get back to winning ways at home.”


              Tennessee put starting guard Fernando Carmona Jr. on injured reserve this week with a foot injury. That doesn't make quarterback Cam Ward's job any easier. Baltimore has problems of its own on the offensive line after losing its top three options at center already. It'll be up to Lamar Jackson to keep the offense functional — and up to the Titans to try to contain him.


              “It’s four guys for six gaps and an elite runner. So he’s elite in that regard and finding open lanes and finding ways to scramble and create off schedule,” Tennessee coach Robert Saleh said. “But it’s always a challenge going against him. We feel good about the speed we have on our D-line and hopefully our rush and coverage match and we got a chance to run them down.”


              Need to know
              T

articles.headline: Minkah Fitzpatrick healthy, ready to rejoin Jets. vs. Bears
articles.description: After suffering a groin injury in Week 1, Minkah Fitzpatrick said he will be back on the field with the Jets on Sunday against the Bears.
articles.headlineJa: ミンカー・フィッツパトリックが回復、ベアーズ戦でジェッツに復帰へ
articles.descriptionJa: 第1週に股関節を負傷したミンカー・フィッツパトリックは、日曜日のベアーズ戦でジェッツのフィールドに戻ってくると語りました。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- After an abbreviated debut with the New York Jets, former All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick is poised to make his re-debut Sunday.

Fitzpatrick, who missed two games after injuring his groin on the sixth play of the season opener, practiced fully Thursday and proclaimed himself ready to play against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field.

He will rejoin a secondary mired in a historic interception drought. The Jets have gone 20 consecutive games without an interception -- 632 pass attempts, to be exact.

"It would be very nice, very sweet" to make the slump-busting interception in his return, Fitzpatrick said with a smile.

It was a frustrating September for Fitzpatrick, one of the Jets' key offseason additions. He was acquired from the Miami Dolphins in a trade and signed a three-year, $40 million contract.

Then came opening day against the Tennessee Titans.

"I started watching film on Tennessee probably in June, so I felt really, really locked in, really in tune with how the game was going to go and how it was going to flow," Fitzpatrick said. "And then six plays in, what happened happened.

"I tried my best to finish the game, but as a DB with the groin, it's kind of tough. So it was frustrating, but also at the same time, you still have to stay locked in. You can't be mad in those circumstances. I was still trying to help the teammates in the best way we can."

The Jets (1-2) have performed reasonably well without Fitzpatrick, who was replaced in the lineup by former starter Andre Cisco. Their defense is second in yards allowed (258 per game) and 12th in scoring (20.3 points), but it has only one takeaway -- a fumble recovery in Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers.

It's a familiar theme; the Jets had only four takeaways last season, a league mark for futility.

"I look at it like this: We just have to keep scratching, clawing and fighting and they'll come our way," said coach Aaron Glenn, the defensive playcaller this season.

The Bears still haven't announced whether Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent will start in place of the injured Caleb Williams (hamstring). The Jets say they're preparing for both backups.

They know Ben Johnson's offense can be confusing, with its myriad formations and pre-snap motion. Fitzpatrick, a three-time first-team All-Pro, is a cerebral player who can be a steadying presence in the secondary.

"I think A.G. has gotten in a groove and has really figured out what he wants us to be as a defense in regards to schematics," Fitzpatrick, 29, said of Glenn. "So I think this week would just be the week that all things are clicking."

articles.headline: Panthers defense looks to slow down Jared Goff and the Lions while missing both starting cornerbacks
articles.description: — The Carolina Panthers found themselves in a precarious position last November, facing a red hot Matthew Stafford without three defensive starters, including standout cornerback Jaycee Horn.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズ守備陣は先発コーナーバック2人を欠く中、ジャレッド・ゴフ率いるライオンズの勢いを止めることを目指す
articles.descriptionJa: — カロライナ・パンサーズは昨年11月、主力CBジェイシー・ホーンを含む守備の先発3人を欠く中で、絶好調のマシュー・スタッフォードと対戦するという危険な状況に直面しました。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — The Carolina Panthers found themselves in a precarious position last November, facing a red hot Matthew Stafford without three defensive starters, including standout cornerback Jaycee Horn.


              But the double-digit underdog Panthers defied odds that day, forcing three Stafford turnovers and getting three touchdown passes from Bryce Young to knock off the Los Angeles Rams 31-28.


              The Panthers (1-2) will look to borrow a page from that playbook Sunday night when they host Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and the rest of the high-powered Detroit Lions offense.


              Carolina's defense is once again ravaged by injuries.


              The Panthers placed starting cornerbacks Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve Wednesday. They'll both miss about eight weeks.


              “People say next man up, and that’s really what it is,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. “I go to the excitement for the opportunity for the guys that are going to play. These opportunities are few and far between, and so ... when guys have a chance to come in and contribute to the team, it changes them. It energizes them."


              The Panthers will turn to Akayleb Evans and rookie Will Lee III to fill those spots, leaving them thin on experience in the secondary. Evans has started 15 games — but only two since 2024 — while Lee makes his first start.


              Will Carolina's successful game plan vs. Bijan Robinson work against Gibbs?
              The Lions (2-1) present a huge challenge for the Panthers defense with Gibbs. 


              He's averaging more than 100 yards per game on the ground with four touchdowns rushing. He also has 18 receptions for 165 yards with two more TDs.


              The Panthers were able a slow down a similar high-profile running back in Week 2, limiting Atlanta's Bijan Robinson to 81 yards from scrimmage while keeping him out of the end zone in a 34-3 win. A similar game plan is expected Sunday night.


              The difference is the Lions have Goff at quarterback, as opposed to Cooper Rush.


              Young excelling through three games for Panthers
              Carolina appears better equipped this season on offense should this game morph into a shootout, which is entirely possible given that the Lions offense has scored at least 31 points in all three games and their defense is surrendering a league-high 31.7 points per game.


              Young is also off to the best start of his career.


              He leads the NFL in yards passing and has seven TD passes. Under Young, the Panthers are in the top seven in the league in scoring and total offense.


              Need to know
              Detroit (2-1) at Carolina (1-2).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m., EDT, NBC.


              Latest odds: Lions by 3 1/2.


              Against the spread: Lions 0-2-1, Panthers 1-2.


              Last week: Lions beat Jet

articles.headline: 76ers envision LeBron James' role being 'offense creator'
articles.description: Sixers coach Nick Nurse envisions LeBron James setting the table for the offense this season. "I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said.
articles.headlineJa: 76ers、レブロン・ジェームズの役割を「オフェンスの創造者」と構想
articles.descriptionJa: シクサーズのニック・ナースHCは、今季レブロン・ジェームズがお膳立て役を担うことを見込んでいます。「私は彼を素晴らしいオフェンスの創造者だと考えている」とナースHCは語りました。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- It took until Day 3 of training camp for Philadelphia 76ers coach Nick Nurse to introduce offensive schemes to his new group.

And though the offense flowed with expected ease Thursday during 5-on-0 drills, role definition will be as important as understanding the playbook when the real games start.

Nurse detailed the offensive responsibilities he envisions LeBron James occupying. The team will certainly put the ball in the 24-year veteran's capable hands -- as, team sources told ESPN, Philadelphia discussed playing James at point forward this offseason -- but he won't be the only one with the ball.

"We got several guys that what I would call 'grab-and-go,'" Nurse said. "If they get rebounds and their first advantage is to start pushing it up the floor and it stays that way, then they're going to do it."

Beyond James, the group Nurse will rely on to push the team in transition includes fellow starters Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Though Nurse emphasized defense during the first two days of camp, part of the presentation was imploring his players to get stops to spark fast-break opportunities when scoring will come instinctively.

When the Sixers set up in the half court, however, Nurse is glad to have James, who ranks No. 1 in all-time points and No. 4 in all-time assists on this team.

"I just think LeBron, I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said. "I don't necessarily mean scorer, I just think creator and a table setter and all that kind of stuff. ... If it isn't bringing it up and starting [the possession], it's probably going to be first pass anyway to [him on] the wing and then we get into our actions, and he's kind of seeing what's there, and he's creating offense for others."

As the Sixers look to organize themselves against a set defense, that's when player recognition will be paramount.

James, Brown and Joel Embiid, for instance, can operate out of the post to initiate offense. The court, however, can get awfully crowded if the team has a player planted on either block and any of those three expect their touches there.

"One, it's a feel thing, and two, we just try to establish some spacing," Brown said. "We try to establish position on the floor, like the style of play. I think we're still kind of figuring it out. Like when I am going to go, when not to go, when big fella is going down in the post, when I can put pressure on the rim, just trying to find that balance."

Brown has already spent time with coaches after practice this week, not only practicing fadeaway shots when double-teamed in the post, but also practicing throwing passes to the 3-point line to elude the double.

Sixers player development coaches have been the recipients of those passes, but the idea is for Brown to picture finding one of his star teammates open if he dissects the defense properly.

"I played with a fair share of stretch 5s, and it really complements my game well," Brown said of Embiid.

articles.headline: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict
articles.description: As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. It may be easier said than done.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティの選手やスタッフはプレミアリーグの有罪判決にどう対処しているのか
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティに対する有罪判決の反響がスポーツ界全体に広がり続ける中、クラブ内部のメッセージは「自信を持って平静を保つ」という姿勢です。しかし、それは言うほど簡単ではないかもしれません。
articles.body:
The strength of the judgement against Manchester City, following their legal case with the Premier League, has shocked the club, its employees and their players. Most of those inside the City Football Academy (CFA) accept that the verdict -- made public for the first time on Tuesday -- is a worst-case scenario.

There's been speculation and discussion on and off at the CFA for more than three years since the charges were announced in February 2023 about what might happen. It was always viewed internally as highly unlikely that every count of financial misconduct would be proved.

City insist they are innocent -- a message that's come from the top, namely chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano -- and many employees want to give the club the benefit of the doubt. They enjoy working for City and feel that they've been well looked after over the years.

In that respect, many people ESPN spoke for this story with are choosing to believe the conviction of Khaldoon and Soriano. At the very least, the majority of these staff members are prepared to wait until after the appeal is heard before passing judgement.

- Legal explainer: Man City have been charged. Now what?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City come back from seismic scandal

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict ruin Guardiola's legacy?

Many staff members are also fans and as such, they are personally invested as well as professionally. City are a big club and a major employer, but since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, they club's owners have done a good job of creating a family feel and a sense of shared purpose. More than 700 employees attended a UK all-staff meeting in the first week of this three-week international break, while players are away on duty with their national teams.

There is, however, a cloud hanging over the CFA, and the mood in general has been described to ESPN as nervous. Soriano, in his video message to staff on Tuesday, insisted it should be business as usual, but in the absence of any real information about what sanctions might follow, there's genuine worry about what the future could hold.

The same goes for the players. With many of City's senior squad away on international duty, some have had direct contact with the club, while others have not. One agent of a first-team player told ESPN that his client is "calm" about the situation and is happy with the public reassurances offered by senior executives. There is, though, an acceptance that things could change depending on the result of the appeal -- which has yet to be filed, but must be lodged by the close of business on Friday, Oct. 2 -- and any punishment handed down.

Player concerns

Speculation over considerable sporting sanctions is causing the most concern, sources tell ESPN. After all, City's players chose to go to the Etihad Stadium to play in the Premier League and the Champions League while getting the opportunity to win trophies.
